concept.name: Discount zone
concept.definition: In SMC/ICT vocabulary, the lower half of a 'dealing range' — the leg between a significant swing low and swing high — i.e., everything below the 50% midpoint. The convention frames longs taken in discount as acceptable value and shorts in discount as poor value; a positioning heuristic, not a valuation measure.
concept.intuition: Split the range in half; buying in the bottom half means paying less than the range's typical price.
concept.mechanics: Anchor the dealing range at a meaningful swing low and high; the midpoint is equilibrium and the region below it is discount. SMC models look for buy-side setups (bullish order blocks, bullish FVGs) located in discount, aligned with the higher-timeframe bias.
concept.formula: Equilibrium = (range high + range low) / 2; discount zone = prices below that midpoint within the dealing range.
concept.failure_modes: In strong downtrends price keeps getting 'cheaper' without bouncing, so discount buys can average into a falling market; results hinge on discretionary anchor selection.
concept.misconceptions: That discount means undervalued or due to rise; it only means 'below the midpoint of the chosen range', which says nothing about where price goes next.
concept.example: With a dealing range of 1800-1900, a bullish order block at 1825 lies in discount (below the 1850 equilibrium), qualifying it — under SMC convention — as a long-entry zone.
